_comment: Authoritative per-size figures for futures products, transcribed from
supplied prose without interpretation. Dollar values stay dollars here;
db/build-futures-catalogue.ts converts them to the percentages the schema
stores, against the size on the same row. Nothing is derived across sizes.
`price` is per size and belongs to that size only. `billing` is `monthly`
where the firm charges a recurring subscription — Take Profit Trader,
TradeDay and Funded Futures Family do. Recording that matters: a $125/month
evaluation and a $69 one-off are not comparable on price alone.
`daily` omitted means no daily rule, which is what the engine reads.
`dailyUnknown` means a daily rule exists without a published figure — that
cannot be left silently blank, so the row says so.
`uncertain` marks products the source explicitly declined to pin down.
Where the two supplied lists disagree, the later one wins and the earlier
sizes are deliberately NOT restored. Do not 'fix' these back:
Top One Ignite      — 50K/100K/150K; the 25K was dropped in the update
Take Profit Trader  — 50K/75K/100K/150K; the 25K was not in the priced list
Traders Launch      — 100K/200K, the only sizes given concrete figures
DayTraders S2F      — 50K only
The5ers Futures     — Day Trade and Swing at 25K/50K, replacing a generic ladder
Firm names are the brand that actually sells the futures product, not the
group that owns it. The supplied list said `AquaFunded Futures`; the firm
trades as AquaFutures (aquafutures.io), the futures division of the
AquaFunded group, and the aggregator export lists it under that name too.
Carrying both spellings produced two firms in the catalogue for one
company, so this file uses the trading name and db/convert-propfirmmatch.ts
maps the alias.
